judged_text: The literal string "refresh_token" is persisted as the credential's refresh_token whenever the parsed response lacks one, overwriting whatever refresh token was previously stored. The real refresh token is destroyed in the database on the first shared refresh, so toggling credential sharing off later — or running with sharing on but CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT unset, which silently falls back to the local refreshFunction — leaves every synced credential permanently unable to refresh without per-user re-authentication; the env toggle is a one-way door.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when the parsed token response lacks `refresh_token`, the code forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the returned parse result is spread into the stored credentials (`o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`), so this placeholder value will overwrite the real previously-stored refresh token whenever the refresh response omits it (a common OAuth behavior). That is persistent data loss and can prevent future refreshes if credential sharing is later disabled or if a normal refresh path is needed. (Salesforce explicitly preserves the old refresh token, but Office365 does not.)
